workflow.selector_prompt: Select the single Quecto repository workflow template, 'feature', before checking steps. If this is the post-completion handoff, first query the issue tracker for issues authored by the authenticated user only (for GitHub: gh issue list --author @me) and choose only from that filtered set.

templates.label: Feature
templates.description: New capability with local hook verification, BDD/TDD, code review, and merge.
templates.when_to_use: Use for all Quecto development work in this repository.
templates.shared_guidance: Shared sub-agent review mechanic (used by both the `bdd_review` and `reviewers` steps): launch each reviewer with `spawn`, binding it to its OWN dedicated review workflow via `workflow_spec`/`template` (never this feature workflow). Spawned reviewers are auto-awaited — you automatically receive a one-line completion note for each at your next idle turn, so an explicit `agent_cmd` `command: 'await'` is optional; use it only if you must block before doing anything else. When you need a reviewer's findings to proceed, read them with `get_messages` (after its completion note, or after an explicit await). Record each spawned sub-agent id for the cleanup step.

steps.label: Install/check local quality hooks
steps.guidance: Run scripts/install-hooks.sh, then verify pre-commit, pre-push, and the git --no-verify wrapper are installed/active before editing code. Never bypass hooks with --no-verify. Done when all three hooks are installed and active.

steps.label: Update Scenarios / Add new features
steps.guidance: Update BDD feature files and task-facing scenarios first, and identify explicit, checkable acceptance criteria for the change. The acceptance criteria identified here are the SAME checklist the later `conformance` step verifies against the branch code, so make them concrete and testable. Done when the scenarios are updated and the acceptance criteria are written down.

steps.label: Write/update unit tests (run a quick smoke check; full suite runs on push)
steps.guidance: Write or update the unit tests for the change. Run a quick targeted smoke check to confirm they compile; the full suite and coverage run on push. Done when the new/modified tests compile and target the new behaviour.

steps.label: Ensure new/modified tests FAIL (RED) — quick targeted run only, not full suite
steps.guidance: Run only the new/modified tests to confirm they fail before any implementation. Done when the new tests fail for the expected reason. If it fails to fail — i.e. a new test passes before implementation — it isn't exercising the new behaviour, so fix the test.

steps.label: Despatch BDD sub-agent to review BDD feature, step tests and unit tests
steps.guidance: Using the feature template's shared sub-agent review mechanic (the `shared_guidance` field), run an independent BDD/test-quality review (its OWN review workflow, not this one). Give the reviewer the issue details, the changed BDD feature files, step tests and unit tests, and its single dimension 'BDD/test quality': verify scenarios follow BDD best practice (clear Given-When-Then, explicit and testable acceptance criteria, one logical scenario per feature, no implementation detail in steps, appropriate step abstraction and reuse), and that unit tests are behavioural, well-named, focused and assert the right things. The reviewer must be skeptical (report only real issues), must NOT modify code, and must return file:line findings with severity, the problem and a concrete fix. Fix any valid concerns before the GREEN step. Done when the BDD review has returned and valid concerns are fixed.

steps.label: Implement code (GREEN)
steps.guidance: Write the code needed to satisfy the failing tests. Do NOT worry about the size of a change — implement it in full. Done when the previously-failing tests pass.

steps.label: Refactor
steps.guidance: Tidy only what this change touches — naming, duplication, clarity. Keep it minimal; no speculative abstraction or unrelated cleanup.

steps.label: Ensure tests still pass
steps.guidance: Run `cargo fmt` and a targeted `clippy -D warnings` locally first (the push gate fails on both), then re-run the targeted tests and confirm GREEN. Respect the file-size cap and strict clippy before pushing. Done when targeted tests pass and fmt/clippy are clean. If it fails, fix the code — never silence clippy — before pushing.

steps.label: Commit
steps.guidance: If on the default branch, create a feature branch first. Stage only the files you changed (`git add <paths>`); never `git add -A` or `git add .` — that sweeps untracked tooling (e.g. `.claude/`) and build artifacts (e.g. `target*/`) into the commit. Write a clear, descriptive commit message and include any commit trailers your harness requires. Done when only the intended files are staged and committed on a feature branch.

steps.label: Push (pre-push hook will run tests and linting)
steps.guidance: Push triggers the full local gate: fmt, strict clippy, unit/architecture/contracts/repo_docs, the 24-shard non-real BDD suite, region coverage at or above the project threshold (quecto and quecto-tui), machete and deny. The zero-cost mocked `@mock-llm` e2e lane runs by default; the live LLM suite (tagged `@manual-real-llm`) is opt-in via `QUECTO_RUN_REAL_LLM=1`. The `find.feature` "Nested .gitignore … in git repo" scenario is load-flaky under the parallel shard wave — re-run the shard before treating it as a real failure (it passes in isolation). Fix every failure; never use --no-verify. Done when the full gate is green. If it fails only on the flaky find.feature scenario, re-run the shard; otherwise fix the failure.

steps.label: Create PR
steps.guidance: Open the PR against the default branch with gh, with a clear title and a body that summarizes the change. The required CI checks are "Unit Tests" and "Mock LLM E2E Tests". Do not claim to co-author it. Done when the PR is open and the required checks are running.

steps.label: Despatch sub agents in parallel as reviewers (Architecture, Security and Performance)
steps.guidance: Using the feature template's shared sub-agent review mechanic (the `shared_guidance` field), dispatch the reviewers in a SINGLE parallel batch (one message, multiple subagent calls) so they run concurrently, each bound to its OWN `review-pr` workflow and given only the PR number, the head commit SHA, its single review dimension and the file scope. Dimensions: at minimum Architecture, Security and Performance; add Correctness and Test-quality for larger changes. Each reviewer reads the diff with gh pr diff <PR>, is skeptical (report only real issues) and must NOT modify code. Every reviewer MUST post findings as INLINE review comments on the PR via the GitHub GraphQL API (gh api graphql) — not a summary, not just a returned report: fetch the PR node id and head SHA with gh pr view <PR> --json id,headRefOid, then submit one review carrying inline comments using the addPullRequestReview mutation (event COMMENT, with a comments array of path/line/body entries anchored to the head commit) or addPullRequestReviewThread per finding. If a line anchor is rejected (line outside the diff, or the PR is already merged), fall back to a review comment that still cites file:line — inline is the default. Each finding states file:line, severity, the problem and a concrete fix. Verify the findings were actually posted on the PR before the fix step. Done when every reviewer has posted inline findings on the PR.

steps.label: Fix all valid review concerns
steps.guidance: Triage each inline finding — confirm it is genuinely valid before changing anything (reviewers can be wrong). Fix forward in the same branch. Track which findings you accept versus decline; you reply to all of them in the resolve step. Done when every valid finding has a fix in the branch.

steps.label: Push changes to remote
steps.guidance: Push the fixes; the full pre-push gate runs again. Wait for it to pass before resolving threads.

steps.label: Reply to the reviewers comments on the PR and mark resolved (use graphql)
steps.guidance: Reply to EVERY review comment on the PR — for accepted findings note the fix and commit, for declined ones explain why — then resolve each thread with the GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation. Thread ids come from the PR reviewThreads connection. Done when every review thread is resolved.

steps.label: Verify the PR meets every issue acceptance criterion
steps.guidance: Systematically verify EACH acceptance criterion from the issue (the same checklist captured in the `scenarios` step) against the ACTUAL branch code, citing file:line evidence. A criterion counts as met only when the evidence is in the code — never on the PR description's claims; be skeptical. Output a per-criterion table marking each met/partial/unmet with its file:line evidence, then a final verdict line: `CONFORMANCE: PASS` only if every criterion is fully met, otherwise `CONFORMANCE: FAIL` listing the gaps. On `CONFORMANCE: FAIL`, fix the gaps and re-verify before merging — do NOT merge on a FAIL. Done when the verdict is `CONFORMANCE: PASS` with file:line evidence for every criterion.

steps.label: Confirm the pre-push gate passed (real-LLM, machete, deny run on push)
steps.guidance: Confirm the latest push's pre-push gate passed in full (coverage threshold, machete, deny, and the mocked `@mock-llm` e2e lane that runs by default; the live LLM suite is opt-in via `QUECTO_RUN_REAL_LLM=1`) and the required CI checks "Unit Tests" and "Mock LLM E2E Tests" are green. Also confirm the reviewers actually POSTED inline findings on the PR (not just a returned summary) and that all review threads are resolved. The `find.feature` "Nested .gitignore … in git repo" scenario is load-flaky — re-run the shard before treating it as a real failure. Done when the gate and required checks are green, inline findings were posted, and all threads are resolved.

steps.label: Merge
steps.guidance: Merge with gh pr merge <PR> --merge --auto --delete-branch (auto-merge waits for the required "Unit Tests" and "Mock LLM E2E Tests" checks). The default branch is protected with enforce_admins; do not force or bypass. Do NOT merge (and do NOT set auto-merge) if any review, fix, or conformance step ERRORED or did not actually run, or if the push bypassed the local gate with --no-verify — a bypassed gate does not count as passing; re-push cleanly or stop and report instead. Done when the PR is merged and the branch is deleted.

steps.label: Move to local master and pull
steps.guidance: Run git checkout master and git pull --ff-only to sync the merge locally.

steps.label: Clean up sub agents
steps.guidance: Reviewers that have already reported completion (you received their one-line completion notes) have exited and need no cleanup. Check `get_subagents` for any sub agent still running, and only then terminate the stragglers (use agent_cmd to abort, or kill each) so no orphaned sub agents remain.

guards.message: Complete hook setup and RED/GREEN work before committing.

Complete code review, pass the conformance gate (CONFORMANCE: PASS), and verify the pre-push gate genuinely passed (not bypassed with --no-verify) before merging. If any review/fix/conformance step errored or did not run, do not merge — stop and report.
